subject.title: [Feature/RFC]: Add eval-backed option discovery to avoid premature convergence in route/strategy answers

question: Should OpenClaw make option discovery before confident route, strategy, or choice recommendations a default invariant across default runtime routes, or keep it as an opt-in research/best-insight behavior?
rationale: The issue is credible and user-impacting, but current main has no established contract or eval, and the default behavior affects cost, latency, runtime prompt boundaries, and Codex/OpenClaw scope.

options.title: Adopt Eval-First Default Invariant
options.body: Accept the invariant in principle, add a generic QA scenario first, then implement the smallest shared prompt/runtime contract needed to pass it.

options.title: Keep Default Lean, Make It Opt-In
options.body: Close the default-behavior request and pursue a research or best-insight profile where extra option discovery is expected.

options.title: Defer Until Search-Depth Work Lands
options.body: Wait for adjacent web_search controls to mature, while keeping this issue open as the canonical behavior-quality RFC.

recommendation.title: Adopt Eval-First Default Invariant
recommendation.body: Accept the invariant in principle, add a generic QA scenario first, then implement the smallest shared prompt/runtime contract needed to pass it.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans prompt behavior, Codex runtime projection, and search observability, and vincentkoc has recent merged work in those adjacent areas.
